partners.mechanism_chain: HES7 (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Spondyloschisis (HP:0004401); PSMB4 (HGNC:9748) —DISRUPTS→ Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammation (HP:0011107); HES7 (HGNC:4892) —DECREASES→ Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508). HES7, a transcriptional repressor, is known to indirectly influence proteasome function. Haploinsufficiency of HES7 may lead to dysregulation of proteasome components or activity, contributing to the spectrum of phenotypes observed in spondyloschisis. Concurrently, direct loss-of-function mutations in PSMB4, a core component of the 20S proteasome, directly impair proteasomal degradation, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and triggering autoinflammatory responses characteristic of proteasome-associated autoinflammatory syndrome 3. The convergence occurs at the level of proteasome function, where both genes, through different mechanisms, impact the integrity and activity of this essential cellular degradation pathway.
